NFL Matchup Cheat Sheet • Season 2026 • Week 9

Generated 2026-11-06 05:06 PM EST

Who's set up for a big week — and why.

A weekly cheat sheet. We grade every starting quarterback, running back, receiver, tight end and defense on how good their spot is this week — not how good the player is. A star facing a shutdown defense in a slow, low-scoring game can be a worse play than a solid guy facing a leaky defense in a shootout. This finds those spots.

How to read a card

  • Grade A+ → D — how favorable the matchup is. A+ = elite spot, D = avoid.
  • Big number (0–10) — the same thing as a score. Higher is better.
  • Projected yards — what we expect this week, adjusted for pace, matchup and expected points.
  • TD chance — odds he finds the end zone at least once.

The five things behind every grade

  1. Matchup — how generous that defense is to this position
  2. Scoring environment — how many points Vegas expects
  3. Production — what he actually did last season
  4. Pace — how many plays the game should run (more plays = more chances)
  5. Usage — how much of his team's work he really gets

Then adjusted for injuries, weather and wind.

How to use it: tap any game in the slate below to zero in on just those two teams. “Who Has the Edge” gives a plain-English read on every matchup — who's favored and where each side wins.

Which season: every team and player stat on this board is the 2025 season — defensive ranks, pace, production, usage. One or two weeks of the new season is too little to trust, so last year stays the baseline until enough 2026 games are in to blend them. Injuries, lines, props and weather are live this week.

Where the numbers come from: ESPN (schedule, stats, injuries, DraftKings lines) · nflverse (snap counts, efficiency) · Open-Meteo (weather). All free, refreshed every time it runs.

Matchup analysis, not betting advice. Lines are shown for reference — place anything you like on DraftKings.
